transcript:
Meeting Header:
Date: 2026-03-25
Time: 15:00 UTC
Duration: 52 minutes
Attendees: Ava Chen (Redwood AE), Diego Ramos (Redwood SE), Maya Patel (Sierra Health Head of Data), Ethan Cole (Sierra Security Architect), Lena Ortiz (Sierra PM)

Summary:  
Quick POC scoping focused on data handling: PII concerns, logging and redaction options, retention settings, and prompt storage. Discussed hosted vs private tradeoffs for the benchmark; agreed to run private deployment benchmark with sample redacted data and to exchange security docs.

[00:00] Ava: Hey everyone, thanks for making time. quick intro, I'm Ava, account exec on this. Diego's our SE, he'll own the benchmark and the config details.
[00:18] Diego: hi all, quick wave. we'll dig into data handling and how the POC would look.
[00:25] Maya: thanks. we wanted to focus on how you handle PII in the logs and whether prompts are persisted. our compliance team is picky about PHI storage so we need detail.
[00:36] Ethan: yes, specifically encryption at rest, KMS, and audit logs. also retention — we can't keep anything longer than 30 days without a signed reason.
[00:47] Lena: timeline wise we want a quick POC in april, two weeks for run, then a decision meeting.

[01:05] Ava: great. high level: Redwood supports hosted, dedicated, and private. for PHI-heavy workloads you usually see customers prefer private (VPC/on-prem) for full control, but we also have hosted options with strict retention and redaction rules.
[01:22] Maya: can you give specifics on what "strict" means? for example, do you store prompts, model outputs, or token-level logs?

[01:35] Diego: yes. default for hosted is that we store request and response logs for debugging for up to X days, and you can opt out. but for PII we have redaction pipelines that mask common PHI patterns. we also support a no-logs option and a minimal metadata-only retention. (paraphrased)
[01:58] Ethan: what's the redaction accuracy? regex won't catch everything.
[02:05] Diego: good point. our redaction is layered: regex for SSNs/dates/phones, NLP-based entity masking for names and medical identifiers, and a final human-review flag if a confidence threshold is low. accuracy is workload-dependent; for structured forms it's high, for free-text clinical notes it can miss edge cases. we recommend pre-processing with customer rules for the POC.

[02:38] Maya: are prompts stored in cleartext in the key-value cache or anywhere? we heard some vendors store prompts for vector indexing.
[02:48] Ava: we never store prompts in vector DBs by default unless you enable embeddings for retrieval. for the runtime, transient KV cache exists in memory for generation and is not persisted to disk in our private deployment. there was a podcast where someone called it K-V cash, not cache — ha.
[03:10] Ethan: ok memory-only KV cache is good. but for hosted, do you persist to logs?
[03:17] Diego: Hosted can persist request/response logs to help debug latency or quality regressions, but you can request logs be redacted or disabled for the POC. retention on hosted can be set to 0, 7, 30 days depending on contract.

[03:35] Lena: if we run the POC in private, what's the installation footprint and the time to get a benchmark running?
[03:43] Diego: typical private POC uses a small cluster — 4 GPUs for model inference on our standard Llama-2-like family for throughput testing. set up is usually 2-5 business days for infra and network, then 1 week for baseline benchmarks. for your timeline, two week run looks feasible.

[04:08] Maya: for sizing, our expected peak is 120 concurrent sessions at 5 RPS each, average prompt length 600 tokens, target tail latency 300ms 95th. Are those numbers realistic?
[04:23] Diego: that maps to quite a bit of GPU memory; we'll simulate with a mixed workload. bench plan: measure p95/p99 latency, token throughput, and cost per 1M tokens. we'll define traffic shape and prompt mixes.

[04:45] Ava: can you confirm success criteria? often customers define success as: 1) p95 under X ms, 2) cost per 1k tokens under Y, 3) no persistent PII retention. what are your must-haves?
[04:59] Lena: must-haves are: PHI not stored beyond 30 days, ability to disable logs during test, and p95 under 400ms. Nice-to-have is model quality parity with our current vendor.
[05:12] Maya: also we need audit logs that show who accessed what and when, ideally integrated into our Splunk.

[05:22] Diego: we support forwarding audit events to customer SIEMs; in private you can keep events in your cluster and ship logs. hosted we can forward or provide log export.

[05:34] Ethan: let's talk encryption. we require customer-managed KMS for any persisted artifacts, and TLS+mutual TLS for control plane.
[05:44] Ava: Redwood supports BYOK with KMS integration for private and dedicated. hosted supports customer-managed KMS for key wrap on persisted artifacts. mTLS for VPC connections is standard for private.

[06:00] Maya: when you say persisted artifacts — does that include embeddings or prompt caches if we turn them on?
[06:07] Diego: yes, anything you enable that writes to disk or object storage will be encrypted with the configured KMS. for embeddings stored in index, you can choose to keep them in your environment only.

[06:22] Lena: retention policy example — can you send a document showing how to set retention per route?
[06:28] Ava: yes, we'll send sample retention configs and a short how-to.

[06:35] Maya: regarding redaction: if the model hallucinates a PHI-like entity, is that captured in logs? we want to avoid storing hallucinated PHI.
[06:45] Diego: good callout. hallucinations are handled like normal outputs; if logs are enabled they'd be captured. for POC we'll recommend disabling logging or enabling output redaction only. also you can filter outputs through a post-processor that masks entities before any persistence.

[07:08] Ethan: for the benchmark itself, can we run both hosted and private and compare cost/latency?
[07:14] Diego: yes; we can run a two-arm comparison. hosted gives faster ramp, private gives control. for sensitive PHI, private better matches compliance.

[07:30] Ava: can we confirm the POC scope: run a 2-week benchmark, compare hosted vs private, validate retention and redaction, and produce a report with metrics and recommended config?
[07:42] Maya: yes. that's our ask.

[08:00] Diego: on tooling: Redwood Console will show per-route token counts, a token-level cost breakdown, and you can toggle retention per route. we'll need to provision an account for you.
[08:14] Lena: provisioning is fine. our infra team will need IP allowlist and SSO.

[08:24] Ava: we support SAML SSO and RBAC roles for view/edit. we'll share the SSO setup doc.

[08:32] Maya: any compliance docs upfront? SOC2, ISO, penetration test results?
[08:37] Ava: yes we'll send the SOC2 report, ISO attestation summary, and our recent pen test high-level findings. note some docs require an NDA; we'll include instructions.

[08:50] Ethan: about prompt storage for embeddings: if we create a retrieval layer and store embeddings in your vector DB, who owns the vector DB?
[08:58] Diego: for hosted, we can host vector indexes encrypted at rest and you can opt to purge or export. recommended for PHI is to run the vector DB inside your VPC (private deployment) with us orchestrating, or you host it entirely yourself.

[09:18] Maya: ok. for the POC we'll keep embeddings off and use transient retrieval to avoid disk persistence.

[09:26] Ava: good. let's talk about bench metrics. Diego, walk through the test plan items.
[09:30] Diego: plan: baseline latency and throughput using your prompt set (we'll use a redacted sample). run ramp tests to target peak 120 concurrent sessions, steady-state 20 RPS, spike tests to 200 concurrent. collect p50/p95/p99 latencies, token/s throughput, GPU utilization, and any error rates. we'll also produce cost estimates.

[10:02] Maya: can you simulate real-world prompt length variance? we have short clinician quick queries and long summarization prompts.
[10:10] Diego: yes we'll model a mix: 60% short (50-150 tokens), 30% medium (300-600), 10% long (1k+). that will affect KV cache warmups and batching.

[10:24] Lena: how do you handle metrics privacy in your dashboard? we don't want raw prompt text in the console.
[10:31] Diego: console can be configured to display only token-level stats and hash identifiers for prompts. we can hide raw prompts entirely for your org.

[10:42] Ethan: any chance of model outputs being sent to third-party monitoring?
[10:46] Ava: no third-party sharing without customer opt-in; telemetry for service health may be aggregated and anonymized. we'll note that in the security brief.

[10:56] Maya: a few operational Qs: if we need to purge PII from logs mid-run, can you perform a live purge?
[11:03] Diego: yes, for private we can purge objects in your S3 or storage and rotate keys; for hosted we can initiate data deletion and we have documented processes for purge requests and verification. there is a small delay for propagation.

[11:22] Ava: let's capture the acceptance criteria now. what are the pass/fail gates?
[11:27] Lena: pass if p95 <= 400ms on private infra, no persisted raw prompts, KV cache memory-only, retention configured to 30 days or less, and we can forward audit logs to Splunk.

[11:41] Maya: also security signoff on KMS and SSO integration within 2 weeks after the run.

[11:50] Diego: we'll include those as acceptance criteria in the bench doc.

[12:00] Ava: timeline recap: we'll send docs by 03/27, you send sample data by 03/30, we schedule infra setup week of 04/06, run benchmarks 04/13-04/24, then decision meeting 04/27. sound right?

[12:18] Maya: yes that aligns with internal schedule.

[12:25] Ethan: one more tech detail — network egress. if private on your managed infra, will there be any egress to Redwood control plane?
[12:33] Diego: minimal control-plane telemetry; you can opt for full air-gap in on-prem where control plane is customer-managed; otherwise control plane uses secure channels to our region. we'll document exact endpoints.

[12:45] Lena: for benchmarks, can we get a sample cost analysis template?
[12:49] Ava: yes Diego will prepare a cost per million token estimate and include GPU-hour breakdown.

[13:00] Maya: any recommended redaction pre-processors?
[13:04] Diego: customers often run a light pre-processor extracting structured fields, then pass only de-identified text. we can share a simple Python preproc script.

[13:14] Ava: ok let's go into a few clarifying questions from Ethan on KMS and logs.
[13:18] Ethan: how do you handle key rotation with persisted embeddings or indices? do you support envelope encryption?

[13:25] Diego: yes we use envelope encryption; keys are wrapped by customer KMS. on rotation we re-wrap metadata; for large indices we recommend re-encrypt+swap in a controlled maintenance window.

[13:40] Ethan: and are audit logs immutable?
[13:43] Diego: we append-only them and store integrity hashes; you can export to your SIEM for long-term retention.

[13:52] Ava: quick note: we'll attach the security brief and a sample retention config to the follow-up email.

[14:00] Maya: great. can you also include an example of redaction false negatives and the manual review flow so our compliance folks see the process?
[14:08] Diego: yes we'll add that.

[14:14] Lena: any blockers from our side to start?
[14:17] Maya: we'll need legal to sign the POC terms but that is quick. security needs the docs.

[14:25] Ava: ok next steps recap: we'll send docs (SOC2, retention config, redaction examples) and Diego will draft the bench plan. Sierra provides sample redacted prompts and traffic estimates.

[14:36] Ethan: sounds good. thanks all.

[14:42] Ava: thanks everyone, we'll follow up with the email and calendar invites.

End of transcript.

Recap / Agreed POC scope:
- Two-week benchmark comparing hosted vs private (private recommended for PHI)
- Focus on redaction, retention, KMS, SSO, and audit log forwarding
- Success criteria: p95 <= 400ms, no persisted raw prompts, retention <= 30 days, audit logs to Splunk
